content_preview.title: As PlayStation Sets a January 2028 End Date for Disc Games, the Video Game History Foundation Presses the ESA for a Legal Digital-Preservation Path
content_preview.summary: Frank Cifaldi says downloading Grand Theft Auto VI and hoping it runs in 50 years is not a preservation solution, and asks the ESA for legal ways to archive digital-only games.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Sony will stop manufacturing disc-based PlayStation games starting January 2028, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2207297/playstation-just-struck-a-hammer-blow-to-game-preservation/). The move has drawn a pointed response from the Video Game History Foundation, whose director argues that the loss of discs matters less than the industry's continued failure to give archives and museums a legal way to preserve digital-only games.

editor_notes.content_quality: Tight, well-structured News piece (438 words, in range). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis flow. Correctly foregrounds the Video Game History Foundation's preservation argument rather than treating the disc cutoff as the whole story. Technical and factual depth is appropriate.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both snapshots read from disk and sha256-verified against manifest.json (matched exactly). source-0.html.gz (Engadget, 'PlayStation just struck a hammer blow to game preservation', Kris Holt, July 3 2026, status 200): CONFIRMS the 2028 disc cutoff ('As of 2028, game discs will be a thing of the past for PlayStation'), the closure of PS3 and PS Vita digital storefronts, the FY April 2025-March 2026 digital share ('nearly four-fifths' ~ the article's 'roughly 80 percent'), the 85 percent figure for the Jan-March 2026 quarter, Cifaldi's 'unfortunate news' quote (verbatim), the ESA 'meaningful solutions for archives and museums...' quote (verbatim), and the 'asking museums to download a copy of Grand Theft Auto VI and hope it'll run in 50 years is not a preservation solution' quote (verbatim). It does NOT support the month 'January' — the source says only 'starting 2028'. source-1.html.gz (Kotaku, 'The Video Game Industry's Trade Body Doesn't Want To Talk About Digital Ownership', status 200): CONFIRMS the 'We have attempted to work with the industry's trade organization to find a legal path forward, but they refuse to offer a meaningful alternative' quote (verbatim), the 'meaningful solutions for archives and museums to legally preserve digital-only content and make it accessible for research' quote (verbatim), and that the ESA 'declined to comment on either Sony's move, or the topic of digital ownership more broadly.' Kotaku also says 'starting in 2028' with no month.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All load-bearing claims trace to a cited source except one: the specific month 'January' in 'starting January 2028' (headline and Overview lead) is not supported by either Engadget or Kotaku, both of which say only 'starting 2028' / 'As of 2028.' The year 2028 and the event itself are fully sourced; only the month is invented. Every other specific (80% FY digital share, 85% final quarter, PS3/Vita storefront closures, all four direct quotes, ESA declined-to-comment) is verbatim or a faithful paraphrase of the snapshots. No orphan URLs: both body-cited URLs (engadget, kotaku) are in article.sources; the only other link is an internal cross-reference to prior GTA VI coverage, which exists on main.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Attribution is explicit throughout ('according to Engadget', 'per Kotaku'). No sensationalism or AI self-reference despite the emotive underlying topic.
editor_notes.originality: Original. No prior Machine Herald article covers Sony's disc discontinuation, the PS3/Vita storefront closures, or the VGHF/ESA preservation dispute. Distinct from adjacent gaming coverage in June-July 2026.
concerns: Headline and Overview lead state 'January 2028' but both cited sources say only 'starting 2028' with no month specified. The month is an unsourced/fabricated specific attributed (in the lead) to Engadget. This is a single recoverable specific — the event and year are correct and sourced — so it is filed as a public correction rather than triggering a reject. Both sources are on the allowlist.
Article calls Cifaldi 'director' while Kotaku calls him 'executive director'; Engadget uses 'director', which the article follows, so this is not a factual conflict.
recommendations: Contributor should not add temporal precision (a month) that no source provides; when sources say 'starting 2028', the article should say 'starting 2028'.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, neutral, well-sourced News piece with a single recoverable defect: the invented month 'January' in the 2028 disc-cutoff date, which no cited source supports. The core event, the digital-share figures, the storefront history, and every VGHF/ESA quote are verified verbatim against the two snapshots. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS: publish with a corrections record noting the sources say 'starting 2028', not 'January 2028'.
